title: Minivan-sized Sponge Found off Hawaii Coast

image.attribution: Twilight Zone Expedition Team 2007, NOAA-OE. / Wikimedia Commons / CC-BY-2.0

main_content:
It might be hard to imagine, but scientists found a sponge the size of a minivan in deep waters near the Hawaiian Islands.

The scientists said this sponge is the largest one ever found by researchers. A U.S. government research ship called the Okeanos Explorer found the sponge last year.

The ship was in the Pacific Ocean, off the Northwestern Hawaiian Islands, when the researchers first saw the sponge. Because the sponge is so large, the researchers said it suggests that it is very, very old.

The sponge has a bluish-white color, and looks a little like a huge brain.

Christopher Kelley is a biologist at the Hawaii Undersea Research Lab. He helped with the research project.

“Here’s this animal that has presumably never been encountered before,” he told The Maui News.

The scientists said the sponge measured over 3.5 meters from one end to the other. They said it was from 1.5 to two meters wide. That would make it bigger than the largest sponge ever recorded.

questions.question: Is this the largest sponge found by researchers?
options: Yes, it is the largest sponge ever found.
No, it is smaller than previous finds.
It is among the larger sponges but not the largest.
The size has not been confirmed.
questions.answer: Yes, it is the largest sponge ever found.

questions.question: Has this type of sponge ever been seen before?
options: Yes, it was previously recorded in other locations.
No, it is presumed to have never been encountered before.
Research indicates it might have been seen by divers.
It is a common type of sponge in the area.
questions.answer: No, it is presumed to have never been encountered before.

questions.question: What are the measurements of the sponge?
options: 3.5 meters long and 1.5 to 2 meters wide.
questions.answer: 3.5 meters long and 1.5 to 2 meters wide.
